market.domesticSlice: figures are India-specific; this is a domestic urban/D2C demand story

structureFacts: India's speciality tea market has grown roughly 3x over five years (from ~₹300 crore to ~₹1,000 crore), driven by Gen Z/millennial demand for premium and wellness-oriented teas — a much faster growth rate than the broader, more mature premium tea market (~4.2% CAGR).
Online tea sales grew 9% in 2024 — D2C brands can reach national scale without heavy distributor networks, which matters for a small, single-city-based brand like Namhah.

adoptionStructure.note: A discretionary, premium consumer purchase (plus a B2B HORECA/gifting channel) — not a recurring-replacement or tender-driven market.

peers.name: Vahdam India
peers.note: A much larger, VC-backed D2C specialty tea brand — raised ₹25 crore from SIDBI Venture Capital in March 2025. Scaling carbon-neutral certified exports and single-origin Assam/Darjeeling micro-batches. A significantly better-funded and more prominent competitor in the same single-origin positioning space as Namhah.

drivers: Provenance and traceability — single-estate/garden-direct sourcing as the core value proposition, differentiating from mass-market blended tea.
Wellness/premium positioning appealing to younger, urban consumers.
Online convenience and national reach without physical distribution infrastructure.
customerValue.strongestPredictor: Credible, verifiable provenance story and online distribution reach — brand trust in a category where quality claims are hard for consumers to verify directly.

steps: identify buyer (D2C consumer or B2B/HORECA/gifting buyer)
curate and price single-estate tea selections
win via provenance story and brand trust
manage multi-channel distribution (own site, marketplaces, B2B)
plan sourcing against estate harvest cycles
onboard via own site, marketplace, or B2B relationship
support/retain via reviews and repeat purchase
demand arises from premium/wellness tea interest or B2B need

sources: ExpertMarketResearch, Fortune Business Insights, IMARC Group (India premium/specialty tea market sizing)
Agro & Food Processing (India speciality tea market growth, ₹300cr → ₹1,000cr)
Ken Research (Vahdam India funding, D2C landscape)
